text:
alex.g: Hey team — first-day CI question. I pushed my first branch and kicked off the Buildkite pipeline for repo `redwood/service-embed` and the job fails immediately during the GH auth step. It tries to upload artifacts and I get a 403. Anyone seen this during onboarding?

buildkite-bot: Build #42 failed — step: upload-artifacts (exit code: 1) :x:
```
> Uploading artifacts to https://ci-artifacts.redwood-internal/...
> Response: 403 Forbidden
Error: Post https://api.github.com/repos/redwood/service-embed/releases/xxx/assets: 403 Forbidden
```

zoe: hmm usually 403 at that stage means the Buildkite GitHub App doesn't have permissions on the repo, or the repo wasn't re-authorized after org-level changes. Did you fork the org repo or is it owned by `redwood`?

alex.g: It's in the org (redwood/service-embed), not a fork. I can see the repo in the org UI. I ran `bk buildkite-agent artifact upload` locally and it managed to start, but the server step fails.

michael: @alex.g two quick checks: 1) Confirm the Buildkite GitHub App installation page (https://github.com/apps/buildkite/installations) lists `redwood/service-embed`. 2) If your org recently tightened permissions, the app might need to be re-authorized for private repo access.

alex.g: I tried the installations page — it shows Buildkite installed for "Some repos" and not "All repos". Service-embed is listed.

jen: Can you paste the buildkite pipeline snippet that uploads artifacts? Sometimes we accidentally rely on a token env var that isn't set in the hosted runners. Also check the pipeline has <artifact-upload> steps using the job-level token.

alex.g: snippet:
```
steps:
  - label: ":package: build & test"
    command: ./build.sh
    artifact_paths: "dist/**/*.tgz"
  - wait
  - label: ":ship: publish"
    command: |
      ./scripts/publish.sh
    agents:
      queue: infra-shared
    artifact_paths: "dist/**/*.tgz"
```

alex.g: The error log shows the GH API call failing. publish.sh calls `gh release upload` with `GITHUB_TOKEN` from the pipeline. Maybe that token is missing/limited?

zoe: Ah — Buildkite's integration doesn't inject a full-perms GITHUB_TOKEN by default. For org repos we use the Buildkite app token, but `gh release upload` expects a token with repo scope. In our pipelines we usually set a secret `RELEASE_TOKEN` (personal or bot token) in the Buildkite pipeline env vars. Did onboarding give you a RELEASE_TOKEN?

alex.g: I don't have one. I assumed the pipeline would have it. 

ci-oncall-bot: NOTE: For new joiners, do not create long-lived personal tokens. Request a bot token from eng-infra (see #eng-infra pinned message) or use the release orchestrator job identity.

michael: @alex.g easiest immediate fix: set a temporary RELEASE_TOKEN in pipeline settings with a team bot token (eng-infra can generate), mark it scoped to `repo` and `public_repo` as needed. Longer term, we'll swap to the release-operator service account so tokens aren't person-bound.

sam: I can create a scoped bot token for you. What repo is it for? I'll DM you the rotation details.

alex.g: Thanks! If I add RELEASE_TOKEN to the pipeline env, do I need to restart the build or re-run the particular step?

jen: You need to re-run the build after updating pipeline env. For Buildkite you can re-run the failed job or trigger a new build. Also double-check the pipeline has `secret` set so tokens are not printed.

zoe: Also verify repo settings > Actions > Allow all actions, otherwise `gh` CLI uploads from actions context might be blocked (less common for Buildkite but still worth checking).

alex.g: Re-ran with a temp token and the publish step started to push — progress! :tada: Logs now show HTTP 201 Created for the asset upload.

michael: Nice. Follow-up items: 1) eng-infra to provision a release-bot token scoped minimal. 2) Update the onboarding doc with explicit step: "Request release token or use release-operator". 3) Add a pipeline check to fail early if RELEASE_TOKEN missing.

sam: Provisioning done, sent DM. I'll add on-call rotation notes.

alex.g: Appreciate the help everyone — saved my first-day panic. Will update PR when I replace temp token.

jen: Welcome aboard! Ping me if you want a quick walkthrough on the release flow. :wave:

buildkite-bot: Build #42 (re-run) passed — step: publish :white_check_mark:
